name: Truth Sleuth (Wisconsin Watch × Center for Media Engagement)
what: Crowdsourced misinformation reporting tool with a newsroom fact-checking dashboard, built with UT-Austin's Center for Media Engagement.
pitch: It is multi-newsroom by design — submitters pick which agency receives the report — so WPR could join rather than build, and OEC could route flags into Watch Ledger entries.
access: Built — Wisconsin Watch — free (free reader account to submit; joining as an agency requires contacting Wisconsin Watch/CME)

name: ICE arrests in Wisconsin tracker (news app)
what: Standing news app tracking Wisconsin ICE arrests, framed as 'follow what happens next' rather than a one-off story.
pitch: Same-state peer turning a spike story into a permanent tracker off Wisconsin records WPR can also reach — the exact Ledger pattern, on a beat WPR has no archive for.

name: Beacon Documenters training cohort
what: Second training class put 48 residents from 33 ZIP codes into local government meetings as note-takers.
pitch: Gavel automates meeting summaries but cannot put humans in rooms; the Beacon shows the recruiting and training pipeline — 89 trained since November 2025 — that would give Gavel verified human notes.
access: Audience — The Beacon (Kansas City) — free to read; Documenters-network model, paid stipends to participants

name: VTDigger 2026 General Election Guide
what: Single election guide product combining candidate and race pages, campaign finance data and voting resources.
pitch: WPR already ships results and voter guide tools, but not campaign finance. VTDigger bundles all three under one URL — a concrete gap to close before November.

name: Ask Wisconsin Watch: reader-submitted candidate questions
what: Call-out asking readers to supply the questions the newsroom puts to 2026 candidates.
pitch: A Wisconsin peer is sourcing voter guide content from readers on the same ballot WPR covers, which makes both the questions and the answers shareable.

name: Beacon community survey published as a story
what: The Beacon published its audience survey findings, reporting readers most want money and spending coverage.
pitch: Publishing survey results as a story, not an internal memo, is free trust-building — and it validates that spending accountability, WPR's Settlement and Rent Ledgers, is what readers actually ask for.

name: Sahan Journal × Mixed Blood Theatre housing story call-out
what: Newsroom partners with a theater to collect residents' housing stories for a live community event.
pitch: Rent Ledger holds filings but not testimony. An arts-venue partner supplies a room, an audience and a reason for tenants to talk — cheap reach beyond existing WPR readers.

name: NNS intergenerational dialogues on violence
what: Wisconsin newsroom ran facilitated community dialogues as a reporting method and published the lessons.
pitch: A Wisconsin peer treating convening as reporting, with the method written up. Care Ledger beats — caregiving, crisis response — need exactly this lived-experience layer that records cannot supply.

name: Bridge Michigan executive editor for growth and audience strategy
what: Bridge created a senior editor role explicitly scoped to growth and audience strategy.
pitch: A structural signal, not a routine replacement: growth lives inside the editing chain rather than in marketing. Useful precedent for how WPR scopes whoever owns the newsletter pipeline and jobs board.

name: Michigan police–immigration reporting lookup
what: Searchable tool showing whether a reader's Michigan police department reports migrants to federal immigration agents.
pitch: This is the Ledger pattern applied to a records request: one dataset, one clear answer per town. Wisconsin agencies file comparable detainer and cooperation records, so the build transfers almost directly.
access: Built — Outlier Media; free to read

name: Outlier's published tracking methodology
what: Post explaining how Outlier gathered, verified and caveated records on police cooperation with immigration enforcement.
pitch: WPR's Ledgers ship without a public methodology. Outlier's shows readers where the records came from and what they don't prove — the missing piece funders and partner newsrooms ask for.
access: Built — Outlier Media; free, methodology public

name: ICE arrests of Asian New Yorkers tracker
what: Tracker cutting federal immigration arrest data by ethnicity, surfacing a sharp rise among Asian New Yorkers.
pitch: Same public arrest data other trackers use, sliced a new way — by community rather than geography. A demographic recut turns a static tracker into recurring stories and newsletter hooks.

name: Chicago School Board 2026 voter guide
what: Candidate-by-candidate guide covering one low-turnout school board race, organized by district.
pitch: WPR already builds voter guides. The borrowable move is depth on a single overlooked race instead of thin coverage of the whole ballot — Wausau school board fits exactly.

name: Milwaukee displacement risk dashboard
what: Dashboard mapping which Milwaukee neighborhoods face the highest displacement risk, surfaced by Urban Milwaukee.
pitch: Wisconsin housing data already assembled and public — the closest analog to WPR's Rent Ledger. Built outside the newsroom, so treat this as a data partner rather than a newsroom build to copy.
access: Built — third-party dashboard; free, covered by Urban Milwaukee

name: Cardinal News sustainability recognition
what: Rural multi-county nonprofit newsroom recognized by online local publishers for business sustainability.
pitch: Cardinal covers a rural, multi-county footprint like WPR's and is being held up as a revenue model. Their mix is the most realistic target WPR has to benchmark against.
access: Revenue — Cardinal News; free to read, entry fees may apply

name: 'Follow the money' reader mandate
what: The Beacon published what readers said they most want covered: public money and how it's spent.
pitch: Converts a call-out into a published accountability mandate. WPR's Ledgers already follow money; having readers say so in their own words is the membership and grant argument WPR lacks.

name: 200 readers on local elections
what: Story reporting what 200 readers said matters most to them in local elections.
pitch: A cheap pre-election call-out that sets the coverage agenda and produces a publishable story by itself. Feeds straight into the question set for WPR's voter guide tools.

name: Speed date a Documenter
what: Fast-rotation networking event pairing residents with civic meeting documenters to recruit and retain them.
pitch: Gavel summarizes meetings automatically but recruits nobody. This is a low-cost, repeatable format for finding residents willing to sit in the meetings Gavel flags as important.

name: Legal action as routine newsroom practice
what: Small newsroom recognized for immigration enforcement coverage and for suing over press access.
pitch: A newsroom WPR's size treating litigation as standard practice, not last resort. WPR's court, permit and Fire Watch pipelines all depend on access that can be cut off without warning.

name: Signal Cleveland neighborhood trash call-out
what: Reader call-out asking residents to report trash-strewn spots in their own neighborhoods for a reporting project.
pitch: WPR's Cleanup Ledger already tracks city cleanup actions, but has no reader front door. This is it: residents nominate sites, giving the ledger a steady local-evidence pipeline.

name: How to Vet NYC Public Schools Like a Reporter
what: Step-by-step guide teaching readers to research a public school using the same records reporters use.
pitch: WPR has the trackers but not the teaching layer. A vet-it-like-a-reporter guide turns Watch and Rent Ledgers into a reader skill and repeat visits.

name: Documented's monthly immigration data column
what: Monthly column written by an outside academic data expert rather than staff reporters.
pitch: WPR publishes ledgers but nothing recurring that explains them. Cheap model: hand a standing data set to a named outside expert for a monthly read.

name: Wisconsin Watch AI-and-careers call-out
what: Statewide call-out asking readers how AI is changing their jobs and career decisions.
pitch: Wisconsin peer sharing WPR's readers and funders. WPR runs tools, not topic call-outs; this is a ready template for a Wausau AI-and-jobs ask.

name: Beacon community conversation on Flock cameras
what: Live community event about police Flock cameras, built from one reader's submitted question.
pitch: WPR covers police tech through Fire Watch and the Watch Ledger but holds no events. Shows one reader question becoming a panel, coverage and a mailing list.

name: Beacon Documenters neighborhood observations
what: Documenters assigned to observe neighborhoods instead of meetings, logging closed stores, sidewalks and new businesses.
pitch: A people-powered feed for WPR's Coming Soon tracker, which now relies on staff noticing. Structured street-level observation is exactly the input it needs.
access: Audience — The Beacon · free, Documenters paid

name: Oaklandside guide to other outlets' voter guides
what: Curated index pointing readers to every other local voter guide and endorsement slate.
pitch: WPR already builds voter guides; being the index of all area guides is a day's work that wins search traffic and goodwill from competitors.

name: Beacon City Hall beat expansion
what: Beacon adds a dedicated reporter to deepen municipal government and City Hall coverage.
pitch: Shows where peer newsrooms put new money: municipal accountability. Useful framing for WPR's funder case that Gavel lets one reporter carry a two-reporter meeting load.

name: Mountain State Spotlight audience growth hire
what: Small statewide nonprofit newsroom creates a dedicated audience growth position.
pitch: Comparable size and budget to WPR, and evidence the next hire at newsrooms like this is audience rather than reporting — relevant to WPR's 2027 staffing choices.
